# Topology-only distances between rooted trees

We cover five main ways to measure how different two **rooted** trees are, looking only at their branching pattern. Branch lengths are ignored.

## Setup and the example trees

```{r}
library(ape)

t1 <- read.tree(text = "((A,B),(C,D));")      # the tree in your picture
t2 <- read.tree(text = "((A,C),(B,D));")      # same shape, different pairing
t3 <- read.tree(text = "(((A,B),C),D);")      # ladder shape
ta <- read.tree(text = "(A,(B,(C,(D,E))));")  # rogue-leaf example, before ...
tb <- read.tree(text = "(B,(C,(D,(E,A))));")  # ... and after moving only leaf A

stopifnot(is.rooted(t1), is.rooted(t2), is.rooted(t3), is.rooted(ta), is.rooted(tb))
par(mfrow = c(1, 3)); plot(t1); plot(t2); plot(t3)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot(ta); plot(tb)
```

## 1. Robinson–Foulds (RF) distance

Count the clusters that are in one tree but not in the other: $$
d_{RF}(T_1, T_2) = |\,C(T_1) \setminus C(T_2)\,| + |\,C(T_2) \setminus C(T_1)\,|
$$ where *C(T)* is the set of non-trivial clusters of *T*. For binary rooted trees the maximum is 2(*n* − 2) (in each tree, there are n - 1 internal nodes, and n - 2 partitions), so $$
d_{RF}^{norm} = \frac{d_{RF}}{2(n-2)} \in [0, 1].
$$

```{r}
library(phangorn)
RF.dist(t1, t2, rooted = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)
RF.dist(t1, t3, rooted = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)
RF.dist(ta, tb, rooted = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)
```

## 2. Triplet distance

Any 3 leaves {x, y, z} of a binary rooted tree are resolved in exactly one of three ways: **xy\|z**, **xz\|y** or **yz\|x**. Here xy\|z means x and y share a more recent common ancestor with each other than either does with z. The triplet distance counts the 3-leaf subsets that the two trees resolve differently (Critchlow, Pearl & Qian 1996):

$$
d_{trip}(T_1, T_2) = \#\{\{x,y,z\} : T_1|_{xyz} \neq T_2|_{xyz}\}, \qquad
d_{trip}^{norm} = d_{trip} \Big/ \binom{n}{3}.
$$

```{r}
cluster_sets <- function(tree) {
  pp   <- prop.part(tree)                 # one entry per internal node
  labs <- attr(pp, "labels")
  cl   <- lapply(pp, function(i) sort(labs[i]))
  cl[lengths(cl) < length(labs)]          # remove the root cluster
}
cluster_strings <- function(tree) {
  vapply(cluster_sets(tree), function(x) paste0("{", paste(x, collapse = ","), "}"), "")
}
triplet_resolution <- function(tree, trip) {
  cl <- cluster_strings(keep.tip(tree, trip))  # the 2-leaf cluster, if any
  if (length(cl) == 0) return("unresolved")
  paste0(gsub("[{},]", "", cl), "|", setdiff(trip, strsplit(gsub("[{}]", "", cl), ",")[[1]]))
}

triplet_table <- function(tr1, tr2) {
  trips <- combn(sort(tr1$tip.label), 3, simplify = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    triplet = vapply(trips, paste, "", collapse = ""),
    tree1   = vapply(trips, function(x) triplet_resolution(tr1, x), ""),
    tree2   = vapply(trips, function(x) triplet_resolution(tr2, x), "")
  ) |> transform(differs = tree1 != tree2)
}

triplet_distance <- function(tr1, tr2, normalise = FALSE) {
  tab <- triplet_table(tr1, tr2)
  if (normalise) mean(tab$differs) else sum(tab$differs)
}

triplet_table(t1, t3)
triplet_distance(t1, t3, normalise = TRUE)
triplet_distance(ta, tb, normalise = TRUE)
```

## 3. Generalized Robinson–Foulds

$$
d_{GRF}(T_1, T_2) = |C(T_1)| + |C(T_2)| - 2 \times (\text{total similarity of the best matching}).
$$ If the similarity is 1 for identical clusters and 0 otherwise, this formula gives back ordinary RF exactly. Smith (2020) recommends **clustering information distance (CID)** as the method for similarity.

```{r}
library(TreeDist)
TreeDistance(t1, t3)
TreeDistance(ta, tb)

VisualizeMatching(ClusteringInfoDistance, t1, t3)
VisualizeMatching(ClusteringInfoDistance, ta, tb)
```

## 4. Path-difference distance

For every pair of leaves *i*, *j*, count the edges on the path between them, $p_T(i,j)$. Collect these counts into a vector for each tree and take the Euclidean distance (Steel & Penny 1993): $$
d_{path}(T_1,T_2) = \sqrt{\sum_{i<j} \big(p_{T_1}(i,j) - p_{T_2}(i,j)\big)^2 },
$$ where $$
p_T(i,j) = \text{depth}(i) + \text{depth}(j) - 2\,\text{depth}(\text{MRCA}(i,j)),
$$

```{r}
edge_count_matrix <- function(tree) cophenetic(compute.brlen(tree, 1))
path_difference <- function(tr1, tr2) {
  d1 <- edge_count_matrix(tr1)
  d2 <- edge_count_matrix(tr2)[rownames(d1), colnames(d1)]   # align leaf order
  sqrt(sum((d1[upper.tri(d1)] - d2[upper.tri(d2)])^2))
}

path_difference(t1, t2)
path_difference(t1, t3)
```

## 5. Rearrangement distances

Define a "move" that changes a tree a little. The distance is the **minimum number of moves** needed to turn T₁ into T₂.

**Rooted NNI (nearest-neighbour interchange).** Pick an internal node *u* (not the root) with children *c₁*, *c₂*, and let *s* be its sibling. Swap *s* with *c₁* or with *c₂*:

```         
        p                      p                      p
       / \                    / \                    / \
      u   s       NNI        u'  c1        or       u'  c2
     / \         ---->      / \                    / \
   c1   c2                 s   c2                c1   s
```

Each rooted NNI changes exactly one cluster. That gives a useful bound: **NNI distance ≥ RF / 2**.

**Rooted SPR (subtree prune and regraft).** Cut off any subtree and re-attach it on any other edge, including a new edge above the current root:

```         
       +---+---+                    +---+---+                       +---+---+
     +-+-+   +-+-+   prune D      +-+-+     |    regraft D        +-+-+     |
     A   B   C   D   -------->    A   B     C    above root ->  +-+-+ |     D
                                                                A   B C
     t1 = ((A,B),(C,D))                                         t3 = (((A,B),C),D)
```

Every NNI is a special SPR, so **SPR distance ≤ NNI distance**.

`phangorn::SPR.dist` only available for unrooted trees. The computational cost of these two methods can be large.

```{r}
# Trees as nested lists: a leaf is a string, an internal node is list(left, right)
as_nested <- function(phy) {
  stopifnot(is.binary(phy), is.rooted(phy))
  rec <- function(node) {
    if (node <= Ntip(phy)) return(phy$tip.label[node])
    kids <- phy$edge[phy$edge[, 1] == node, 2]
    list(rec(kids[1]), rec(kids[2]))
  }
  rec(Ntip(phy) + 1)
}
canon <- function(x) {                     # canonical Newick: same tree -> same string
  if (is.character(x)) return(x)
  s <- sort(c(canon(x[[1]]), canon(x[[2]])))
  paste0("(", s[1], ",", s[2], ")")
}
get_at <- function(x, p) { for (i in p) x <- x[[i]]; x }
set_at <- function(x, p, value) {
  if (length(p) == 0) return(value)
  x[[p[1]]] <- set_at(x[[p[1]]], p[-1], value); x
}
all_paths <- function(x, prefix = integer(0)) {
  if (is.character(x)) return(list(prefix))
  c(list(prefix), all_paths(x[[1]], c(prefix, 1L)), all_paths(x[[2]], c(prefix, 2L)))
}

# rooted SPR: cut any non-root subtree, re-attach on any edge of the rest (or above the root)
spr_neighbours <- function(x) {
  out <- list()
  for (p in all_paths(x)[-1]) {
    sub  <- get_at(x, p)
    par  <- p[-length(p)]; sib <- c(par, 3L - p[length(p)])
    rest <- set_at(x, par, get_at(x, sib))             # prune
    for (q in all_paths(rest)) {
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- set_at(rest, q, list(get_at(rest, q), sub))  # regraft
    }
  }
  out
}

# rooted NNI: for internal node u = (c1,c2) with sibling s, swap s with c1 or c2
nni_neighbours <- function(x) {
  out <- list()
  for (p in all_paths(x)[-1]) {
    u <- get_at(x, p)
    if (is.character(u)) next
    par <- p[-length(p)]; s <- get_at(x, c(par, 3L - p[length(p)]))
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- set_at(x, par, list(list(s, u[[2]]), u[[1]]))
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- set_at(x, par, list(list(u[[1]], s), u[[2]]))
  }
  out
}

# breadth-first search from tr1 until tr2 is reached
rearrangement_distance <- function(tr1, tr2, move = c("spr", "nni")) {
  neighbours <- switch(match.arg(move), spr = spr_neighbours, nni = nni_neighbours)
  start <- as_nested(tr1); goal <- canon(as_nested(tr2))
  if (canon(start) == goal) return(0)
  seen <- new.env(); assign(canon(start), TRUE, envir = seen)
  frontier <- list(start); d <- 0
  while (length(frontier) > 0) {
    d <- d + 1; nxt <- list()
    for (x in frontier) for (y in neighbours(x)) {
      key <- canon(y)
      if (key == goal) return(d)
      if (!exists(key, envir = seen, inherits = FALSE)) {
        assign(key, TRUE, envir = seen); nxt[[length(nxt) + 1]] <- y
      }
    }
    frontier <- nxt
  }
  Inf
}

rearrangement_distance(t1, t2, "spr")
rearrangement_distance(t1, t2, "nni")
rearrangement_distance(ta, tb, "spr")
rearrangement_distance(ta, tb, "nni")
```

## Which one to use?

SPR seems the most suitable to measure how recombination events change trees. Triplet distance and GRF might also be useful.
